ORDER Petitioners have filed this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging notification under Section 5(2)(k) of M.P. Krishi Upaj Mandi Adhiniyam, 1972 dated 09.03.2011 and 20.06.2011.

2. Deputy Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department has issued a notification under Section 5(2)(A) of M.P. Krishi Upaj Mandi Adhiniyam, 1972 declaring Khasra No.184/2 measuring 6 acres and Khasra No.183/3 measuring 2 acres to be Sub Mandi Samiti area of Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti Banapura.
Another notification was issued on dated 09.03.2011 declared villages situated in 5 km. periphery to be area of Sub-Mandi Samiti.

3. Counsel appearing for petitioner submitted that areas of aforesaid khasra numbers were acquired by the State Government under Land NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55814 2 WP-13455-2011 Acquisition Act and award has been passed.

sentences.text: Sub Divisional Officer has made recommendation to take up the issue in suo moto revision under Section 50 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code for release of rest of the land of petitioner.
Sub Divisional Officer by its report dated 20.04.2010 has made recommendation for release of land.
It is submitted that proceedings for release of land under Section 48 of Land Acquisition Act is pending at the final stage.
It is submitted that petitioner has not accepted the compensation for acquisition of his land and has returned the award amount.

Counsel for petitioner further submitted that respondents had committed an error in law in issuing notification in respect of land of petitioner declaring it Sub Mandi area of Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti Banapura as Government has recommended for release of land as same is not required and not used after land acquisition.
During pendency of proceeding notifications ought not to have issued and notifications dated 09.03.2011 so far as it relates to land of petitioner is bad in law.
Counsel for petitioner also submitted that possession of land has not been taken.
Petitioners are in possession of land.
Taking of symbolic possession will not suffice for purposes of Land Acquisition Act and actual possession is required to be taken.
Reliance is placed on judgment passed by Apex Court in case of Balwant Narayan Bhagde Vs. M.D. Bhagwat and others; (1976) 1 SCC 700 .

4. Counsel appearing for Mandi Board submitted that no error has been committed in law by issuing notification dated 09.03.2011 declaring the land of petitioner to be Sub Mandi area.

sentences.text: It is submitted that petitioner has never challenged award by which land has been acquired.

In absence of challenge to award by petitioner, now petitioner cannot challenge the notification which has been issued by State Government declaring land to be Sub Mandi area of Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti Banapura.

5. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3 has relied upon judgment passed by Coordinate Bench in W.P. No.5668/2017 wherein reliance has been placed on judgment passed by Apex Court in case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal and others; (2020) 8 SCC 129.

Relevant para of writ petition (supra) is quoted as under:-
"Reading from para 366.7 of the judgment in Indore Development Authority (supra)

,
it is pointed out that once possession was taken as is evident from R-4/6, then in absence of any particular method being prescribed for drawing of inquest report/memorandum, possession will deemed to have taken and land will stand vested in the State as there is no divesting provided under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, as once possession has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55814 4 WP-13455-2011 been taken there is no lapse under Section 24(2).
It is also submitted that there is no provision of automatic or deemed lapse of the acquisition proceedings under the Act of 1894.

In fact, Section 101 of the Act of 2013 has a provision for return of unutilized land but that too is restricted to the lands which have been acquired under the provisions of 2013 Act and proposition has been Smt. Kamla Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Thus, reading from the judgment of Indore Development Authority (supra) itself.

It is submitted that since there is no provision for return of land under the Act of 1894 and land in question was admittedly not acquired under the Act of 2013, therefore,
provisions of Section 101 will not be applicable.

It is further submitted and reading from Annexure R-4/8, there are courses in agriculture for which land is being utilized and once land has vested in favour of the respondents then it cannot be returned.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, certain facts are crystal clear, namely, there is no dispute that compensation as was ascertained by the Land Acquisition Officer was paid to the claimants i.e. the petitioners.
Physical possession was taken over by the State Authorities on 19.04.1968 vide order Annexure R-4/6.

Thirdly, petitioners were keeping silent since 1968 till 2014 i.e. for long 46 years they did NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55814 5 WP-13455-2011 not bother to raise any issue in regard to land so acquired.
As far as power to take possession is concerned, Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 deals with the power.

Law in regard of divesting of acquired land is very clear as held in case of V. Chandra Sekaran & Anrs. Vs.
Administrative Officer & Ors, 2012 (9) JT 260, wherein it is held that once the land is acquired and it vests in the State, free from all encumbrances, it is not the concern of the land owner, whether the land is being used for the purpose for which it was acquired or for any other purpose.

sentences.text: He becomes persona non-grata once the land vests in the State.
He has a right to only receive compensation for the same, unless the acquisition proceeding is itself challenged."

It is submitted that since compensation has already been paid but petitioner has refused to accept the same and possession of land is taken, therefore, proceeding under Land Acquisition Act will not lapse.
No writ of mandamus can be issued declaring proceedings to be lapsed.

It is also submitted that writ of certiorari also cannot be issued since petitioner has not challenged the award and in absence of challenge to award, no case is made out for issuance of writ of certiorari for quashing of notification issued by State Government.
Prayer is made for dismissal of writ petition.
Counsel for respondent submitted that proceedings under Section 48 of Land Acquisition Act for release of land is available during pendency of proceeding where award has not been passed.
In cases where award has been passed and has become final, proceeding under Section 48 cannot be initiated.

Land acquisition process under Act No. 1 of 1894 shall be deemed to have lapsed in certain cases.- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, in any case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894,-
(a) where no award under section 11 of the said Land Acquisition Act has been made,
then, all provisions of this Act relating to the determination of compensation shall apply; or (b) where an award under said section 11 has been made, then such proceedings shall continue under the provisions of the said Land Acquisition Act, as if the said Act has not been repealed.

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), in case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (1 of 1894), where an award under the said section 11 has been made five years or more prior to the commencement of this Act but the physical possession of the land has not been taken or the compensation has not been paid the said proceedings shall be deemed to have lapsed and the appropriate Government, if it so chooses, shall initiate the proceedings of such land acquisition afresh in accordance with the provisions of this Act:
Provided that where an award has been made and compensation in respect of a majority of land holdings has not been deposited in the account of the beneficiaries,
then, all beneficiaries specified in the notification for acquisition under section 4 of the said Land Acquisition Act, shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Act."

sentences.text: Khasra No.183/3 and 184/2 was acquired in land acquisition case No.76/A-82/1971-72 and award was passed on 23.03.1973.
Out of Khasra No.183 only 0.90 acre and out of Khasra No.184 only 1.10 acre, total two acre was to be acquired by Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti, but 8 acres was acquired.
Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti is actually using aforesaid land for public purposes.
Petitioner made representation to return rest of his land.
Report was called and on basis of recommendation made by S.D.O. dated 28.01.2010, proceedings were initiated under Revenue Book Circular Division 1 Chapter - IV for return of land.
Though award amount has been deposited and same was accepted by petitioner and later on award amount was returned and deposited in government treasury.
Possession was with petitioner though symbolic possession has been taken by Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti.
Now, question arises before this Court whether writ of mandamus can be issued declaring the proceeding to have been lapsed.

In case of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55814 9 WP-13455-2011 Manoharlal (supra), Apex Court has held that cases where possession has not been taken for period of five years and compensation has not been paid, in such cases, proceedings under Land Acquisition Act shall lapse.
In the present case, compensation has been deposited with the State Government by the department.
It was also accepted by petitioner, but later on returned.
Possession has been taken and if petitioner again comes in possession, they are encroachers.
14. In view of aforesaid, it cannot be said that proceedings have been lapsed as no compensation was paid to petitioner and possession has not been taken.
Department has already paid the compensation amount, though same has not been accepted by petitioner.
Actual possession of part of the land has also been taken and symbolic possession of rest of the land is taken, therefore, it cannot be said that possession has not been taken.
Due to aforesaid factual matric, case of Manoharlal (supra) will not be applicable and no writ of mandamus can be issued declaring proceedings to have been lapsed.

Another question for consideration before this Court is whether notifications dated 09.03.2011 were bad in law as proceedings have already been initiated under Revenue Book Circular for return of land as land is not required for use by the department.
After passing of award dated 23.03.1973, challenge is not made to said award by petitioners.
No reference was filed before District Magistrate neither any petition was preferred for quashing part of the award in respect of their land.

Land Acquisition Officer has refused to amend the award which has already been passed and has given advise to Collector to initiate proceedings for return of land under Revenue NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55814 10 WP-13455-2011 Book Circular.

Revenue Book Circular lays down that if land is not required by the government and it is required by some other department, then proceedings can be initiated to give the land to said department under Division-I Chapter - IV, Clause (1), (2) and (3).

In case, Clauses (1), (2) and (3)
will not applicable, then Clause (4) will come into operation and land can be returned to the persons from whom same has been acquired or through their legal heirs.
In present case, initially part of the land of Khasra No.183/3 and 184/2 was used and symbolic possession was there over rest of the land.
Though, actual possession was with petitioner, but later on, notification has been issued declaring the land to be of Sub Mandi Samiti of Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti Banapura.

Since notification has been issued, therefore, it is clear that land is required by Sub Mandi Samiti of Krishi Smt. Kamla Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159015590/
6 Upaj Mandi Samiti, Banapura.

sentences.text: Due to publication of notification dated 09.03.2011, it cannot be said that land is no longer required by the department for which it is acquired as notification has already been issued, therefore, now, land cannot be returned to petitioners.

Though proceedings has been initiated by Collector for return the land under said clause, but due to publication of notification dated 09.03.2011, Clause (1), (2) and (3) has become operational and therefore Collector could not rely on Clause (4) for return of land.
In these circumstances, writ petition filed by petitioners is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
No writ of mandamus can be issued declaring proceedings to be lapsed.
In cases where award has been passed and has become final, proceeding under Section 48 cannot be initiated.
Clause (4) of Division I Chapter IV will be applicable if Clause (1), (2)
and (3) are not in operation.
Due to publication of notification dated 09.03.2011, it cannot be said that land is no longer required by the department for which it is acquired as notification has already been issued, therefore, now, land cannot be returned to petitioners.
Though proceedings has been initiated by Collector for return the land under said clause, but due to publication of notification dated 09.03.2011, Clause (1), (2) and (3) has become operational and therefore Collector could not rely on Clause (4) for return of land.
In these circumstances, writ petition filed by petitioners is dismissed.
